On the upper side, a persistent estimator with primal averaging complements accelerated proximal dual steps equipped with an explicit primal certificate. The characterization takes the worst case over admissible known dual domains and finite dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Wendao Wu, Haihan Zhang, Qian Chen, Chenheng Zhang, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin

item.title: Matching Randomized First-Order Bounds for Higher-Order Smooth Nonconvex Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.17074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Does randomization improve the worst-case first-order complexity of nonconvex optimization when the objective is very smooth? We prove that, for every fixed finite integer $p\ge3$, finding an $\eps$-stationary point requires $\Omega_p(\eps^{-5/3})$ exact value-and-gradient queries, even for $C^\infty$ objectives with initial gap at most one and simultaneous global Lipschitz budgets of one for derivatives of orders $1,\ldots,p$. Together with the known deterministic upper bound, this determines the accuracy exponent up to a single logarithmic factor. The lower bound holds for unrestricted adaptive randomized algorithms, unbounded query locations, and outputs that need not have been queried. One algorithm-independent hard distribution suffices in dimension $O_p(\eps^{-47/3})$. The construction combines a block-chain potential with an exact quartic core, repeated quadratic spectra, and two static Gaussian tensor perturbations. A scheduled Haar argument controls the entire adaptive query span. An innovation-only Gaussian comparison then bounds exact transcript information without assuming finite precision or a minimum query separation. This establishes the $5/3$ randomized accuracy barrier under every prescribed finite smoothness order, extending the previously matched third-order case.
item.dc:creator: Haihan Zhang, Wendao Wu, Fangqing Zhang, Chenheng Zhang, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin

item.title: A Feasible Direction Method with Active-Set Identification for Derivative-Free Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.17101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a model-based trust region method for derivative-free optimization with simulation-based inequality constraints. We are motivated by settings of simulation optimization in which both function evaluations at infeasible points may be unreliable and constraint evaluations are expensive. Our method maintains feasible incumbents and computes steps from a subproblem suitable for a feasible-direction method in order to encourage generation of feasible trial points. To reduce the computational cost of modeling the constraints, we describe an active-set estimation scheme that permits modeling with only a subset of constraints in each subproblem, as opposed to maintaining models of all constraints. We show that every limit point of the incumbents generated by our method is a Fritz-John point, and is additionally a KKT point under the Mangasarian-Fromovitz constraint qualification. Under standard nondegeneracy conditions, the active-set estimate identifies, within finite time, all constraints active at the limit point of the incumbents. Experiments on CUTEst problems show that our method generates feasible trial points far more often than a comparable SQP-based approach and solves more problems within a given budget with fewer function evaluations.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Larson, Matt Menickelly, Lara Zebiane

item.title: A Composite Representation Theorem for Solution Mappings in Regularized Composite Optimization with Applications to Hausdorff Lipschitz Stability
item.description: arXiv:2610.17105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the geometry and stability of solution mappings in regularized composite optimization, allowing multiple minimizers. We establish a composite representation that separates optimal linear images from their corresponding primal solutions through an image mapping and a generalized basis pursuit mapping. Under a fiber-attainment condition, the image mapping admits a reduced optimization formulation; neither representation requires convexity. For convex regularizers, suitable qualification conditions yield a Fenchel-conjugate representation of the reduced value function and a geometric characterization of the generalized basis pursuit mapping through affine fibers and a fixed lifting set. Using these representations, we establish sufficient conditions for local Hausdorff Lipschitz continuity of possibly set-valued solution mappings. We further show that the primal-space sufficient conditions imply the corresponding image-space conditions, with an additional injectivity requirement arising in the former. The results cover $\ell_1$-type and structured piecewise linear-quadratic regularizers under suitable assumptions. For classical $\ell_1$ regularization, our approach recovers an existing stability result without a finite sign-pattern decomposition. Numerical examples illustrate the recovery of complete solution sets, including a case with a nonpolyhedral graph of the generalized basis pursuit mapping.
item.dc:creator: Peixuan Yang, Wei Yao, Jin Zhang

item.title: Last-Iterate Convergence of Frank--Wolfe for Nonlinear Variational Inequalities on Polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.17127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Frank--Wolfe algorithm for solving variational inequalities over compact polytopes under a monotone $C^1$ operator $\Phi$. The linear minimization oracle returns vertices, and we assume a coercivity condition on the Jacobian of $\Phi$ at a solution. We prove last-iterate convergence to the unique solution at rate $O(k^{-\min\{\alpha,1\}})$ for step sizes $\gamma_k=\alpha/(k+\beta)$ with $\beta\geq\alpha>0$. The bound holds uniformly over starting points and vertex tie-breaking. In particular, both $1/(k+1)$ and $2/(k+2)$ give $O(k^{-1})$ distance. A matching lower bound shows that this distance guarantee is worst-case order-optimal among prescribed admissible step-size schedules. We also obtain rates $O(k^{-\min\{\alpha,1\}})$ for the Frank--Wolfe gap and $O(k^{-\min\{\alpha,2\}})$ for the dual gap. These yield $O(\varepsilon^{-1})$ and $O(\varepsilon^{-1/2})$ calls to each oracle for sustained gap accuracy $\varepsilon$ when $\alpha\geq1$ and $\alpha\geq2$, respectively, with instance-dependent constants. We also treat more general prescribed step-size schedules.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Harks

item.title: Failure Modes of Interior-Point SDP Solvers on Moment--SOS Hierarchies
item.description: arXiv:2610.17261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standard semidefinite programming (SDP) solvers working in double precision can become unreliable on difficult problems, even when their output appears plausible. We study this issue for SDP problems arising from high-order moment-SOS hierarchies. Three polynomial optimization problems are analysed by comparing standard double-precision computations with reference solutions obtained using the extended-precision solver \mbox{Loraine\,64x4}. We observe two distinct patterns of numerical failure. In \emph{false convergence}, the computed bounds form a smooth sequence but approach the limit at the wrong rate. In \emph{stagnation}, the sequence develops a plateau or oscillations and no longer reflects the convergence of the underlying hierarchy. We introduce an empirical effective condition number based on the positive spectral components of the primal and dual solution matrices. It serves as a warning indicator rather than an error bound, and its growth accompanies numerical deterioration in our examples. We also examine the imbalance between primal and dual spectral conditioning and a Cholesky inverse residuum as potential diagnostic indicators. The results show that solver termination messages and apparently regular convergence curves may be insufficient to establish the reliability of high-order moment-SOS bounds.
item.dc:creator: Michal Kocvara

item.title: Mitigating Performance Variability in Mixed-Integer Programming Solvers via LP State Steering
item.description: arXiv:2610.17268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers repeatedly solve linear programming (LP) relaxations, but the LP state transferred from the simplex algorithm to the branch-and-bound tree is typically treated as an artifact of perturbation, presolve history, and numerical trajectory. This is harmless in pure linear programming, where alternative optimal bases certify the same bound. In MIP, however, those bases can expose distinct fractional structures, active rows, reduced costs, branching candidates, and reoptimization states. The inherited LP state is therefore an initial condition for the integer search. We exploit this initial condition to mitigate computational performance variability. The proposed framework generates alternative LP states on or near degenerate optimal faces, evaluates them within an auxiliary solver environment, and either selects a single state or executes a portfolio of candidate states in parallel. A handcrafted synthetic instance isolates the relationship between the initial LP state, the fractional profile, the branching trajectory, and the resulting node-count distribution: root-state steering reduces the weighted variability score~(WVS) by 67% over 1,000 paired seeds and produces no node-count regressions relative to default SCIP. On a separate 130-instance MIPLIB 2017 validation set with up to 50 paired seeds per instance, the top-five policy improves solve completion from 3,792 to 3,894 runs, reduces the shifted geometric mean of the recorded node count from 2,574.7 to 1,198.0, and lowers the median WVS by 9% on instances reliably solved by the baseline. These results demonstrate that the branch-and-bound phase inherits a specific LP state rather than merely an LP bound, and that the active management of this state systematically mitigates computational performance variability.
item.dc:creator: Mourchid Adegbindin, Brenda Dietrich, Jamol Pender

item.title: Vanishing Events and Regularity-Conditioned Reachability in Linear Stieltjes Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.17345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study linear Stieltjes control systems in which actuation is concentrated at finitely many temporal events, and we ask what happens when one of those events progressively loses its atomic weight in the associated Stieltjes measure. For constant coefficients, ordinary finite-atomic reachability is governed by a truncated Krylov space and is therefore insensitive to the positive values of the event weights. A different picture emerges once trajectory regularity is imposed. In the supercritical super-$g$-H\"older regime, we minimize the largest event-normalized state jump and characterize exactly the terminal directions for which this cost remains uniformly bounded as a prescribed event weight tends to zero. The characterization combines what can be reached before the vulnerable event, a drift-cancellability condition at that event, and the directions that remain available afterwards. Ordinary reachability of the deleted-event system can therefore be strictly larger than bounded-cost reachability in the singular limit. We also separate two mechanisms of divergence: loss of ordinary reachability after deletion and failure of the intermediate compatibility condition. For compatible targets, the minimum cost converges to a constrained deleted-event problem. A dimensionless position--velocity benchmark motivated by pulsed proximity maneuvers shows the distinction explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Francisco J. Fern\'andez

item.title: Global Extendability of Flat Cliques in Sparse Moment Relaxations
item.description: arXiv:2610.17371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moment relaxations provide lower bounds for polynomial optimization problems, while the moment matrix carries more information than the bound itself. When the moment matrix satisfies the flat truncation condition, the bound is tight and global minimizers can be extracted from the matrix. In correlatively sparse relaxations, it is common that only some blocks are flat. We study whether such partial flatness still reveals part of a global minimizer. On a unicycle trajectory optimization problem, repeatedly extracting the atoms of flat cliques and fixing them recovers feasible, near-optimal trajectories. We then construct a counterexample whose relaxation is tight and has a rank-one flat clique, yet the unique extracted atom cannot be extended to a global minimizer. Finally, we give sufficient conditions for global extendability that involve only the boundary of a clique. Every extracted atom minimizes its clique objective given its boundary value, and when the bound is tight and the boundary moment block has rank at most one, the extracted atom of the clique is globally extendable.
item.dc:creator: Haoran Sun

item.title: Beyond periodicity: Fourier methods for optimal control
item.description: arXiv:2610.17386v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fourier-based spectral methods provide compact global approximations, permit simple differentiation and integration, and achieve spectral convergence for smooth periodic functions. Their use in finite-horizon optimal control problems (OCPs) is nevertheless challenged by the generally nonperiodic state and control trajectories: endpoint mismatch induces artificial discontinuities and can destroy spectral convergence. Leveraging Eckhoff-type endpoint-correction techniques, we develop a Fourier-based spectral framework for OCPs with possibly nonlinear dynamics and constraints. The correction improves convergence without enlarging the set of decision variables, yielding an efficient finite-dimensional numerical method. Furthermore, we formulate selected dynamics and obstacle-avoidance constraints through Sobolev residual bounds, which incorporate information about the residuals over the entire time horizon and improve constraint satisfaction. Numerical experiments on benchmark problems demonstrate competitive computational performance, lower residual errors, and improved solution accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Milena Ispiryan, Vahagn Makaryan, Lusine Poghosyan, Tigran Bakaryan

item.title: Spectral Self-Concordant Barriers: A Proof of a Conjecture by Tun\c{c}el
item.description: arXiv:2610.17442v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $Q \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a open, convex, and symmetric set and let $f:Q \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a $\vartheta$-self-concordant barrier function, that is also symmetric. We show the associated spectral function $F(X)= \mathcal{O}^2 (f \circ \lambda)(X)$ is a $\mathcal{O}^2\vartheta$-self-concordant function, where $\mathcal{O} = 8\max\{1+3\vartheta, 12\}$, on the domain of all $n \times n$ symmetric matrices $X$, with eigenvalues $\lambda(X) \in Q$. This generalizes the relationship between the standard logarithmic barriers $-\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i$ and $-\log \det X$ and gives a solution to a conjecture by L.~Tun\c{c}el, 1995.
item.dc:creator: Javier Pe\~na, Hristo Sendov

item.title: Optimal Feature-Based Newsvendor Policies under Censored Demand
item.description: arXiv:2610.17465v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a newsvendor problem where a decision-maker observes a $z$-dimensional vector of covariates, and wants to learn how much stock to order given a sample of size $n$ of censored demand data to minimize costs. Demand is censored when insufficient stock is available to meet it, and past stocking quantities are known. We propose a new model-agnostic loss function approach to estimate optimal order quantities using observational data, and characterize the optimal newsvendor policy as the policy that minimizes our proposed loss function. Our method requires only a single estimation step, can be scaled to datasets with hundreds of thousands of data points, and does not suffer from the same instabilities as inverse censoring probability weighting methods. We describe how this loss function can be implemented in linear empirical risk minimization, kernel weights optimization and deep neural network algorithms, and provide excess risk generalization bounds for their out-of-sample performance. Moreover, we show through numerical experiments that our method quickly converges to the optimal policy on synthetic data, and leads to improved performance on real world retail data.
item.dc:creator: Joost van der Haar, Ilias Willems, Joachim Arts, Ingrid Van Keilegom

item.title: Balancing cost and demand in a smart grid - a mean-field game analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.17477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a smart grid, consumers can also play the role of producers and sellers of energy. Therefore, the control of a smart grid over time becomes a dynamic game with a large number of small players and one or several large players. This is much more complicated than the control of an energy system with a single producer. The framework of mean-field games with common noise allows the transformation of such a complicated model into a control problem for a typical prosumer (producer and consumer in one) optimizing his behavior against a flow of other such prosumers. In our model, we introduce 2 decision variables for such a controller: one describing the amount of electric energy bought from the grid (or sold to it), and the second one describing the charging rate for our battery. The cost function is designed to satisfy two goals: satisfying the demand of the consumer (a single home) and minimizing the payment for energy. Players are allowed to sell/buy energy from the grid. Common noise is hidden in price volatility and sun irradiance, which influence all the players. We compute the optimal controls for our model and simulate solutions on real data. The novelty of our construction, compared to other works on smart grid control, lies in combining the minimization of the cost of energy and sustaining some level of demand satisfaction. We analyze the impact of battery usage on achieving a balance between these two criteria. We also take into account that the smart grid is only part of the energy market, which makes consumer strategies dependent on energy consumption outside the grid.
item.dc:creator: Micha{\l} Jakubowski, Piotr Wi\k{e}cek

item.title: Fundamental Limits of Prescribed-Time Regulation: Gain Budgets, Accuracy Frontiers, and Arrival Costs
item.description: arXiv:2610.17484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prescribed-time controllers drive the state to the origin at a time $T$ chosen in advance, with gains that grow without bound as $t$ approaches $T$. This paper shows the growth is a necessity and computes the exact price of avoiding it. The starting point is a simple estimate: any trajectory with $\|\dot z(t)\|\le L(t)\|z(t)\|$ satisfies $\|z(t)\|\ge\|z(0)\|e^{-\int_0^t L}$. From this: a gain profile $L$ supports exact prescribed-time convergence, over the unrestricted class of closed-loop vector fields admitting it, if and only if its integral over $[0,T)$ is infinite; so every design must either use an envelope of infinite integral or violate the linear growth bound at the origin, as finite-time and fixed-time designs do. Under a finite gain budget $\mathcal B=\int_0^T L$ the best worst-case contraction over the class is exactly $e^{-\mathcal B}$, a floor valid for every plant, and a finite-budget trajectory converges to a definite point away from the origin. A comparison lemma then carries the theory beyond linear growth: for envelopes $\|\dot z\|\le L(t)\,\omega(\|z\|)$, first arrival at the origin requires budget at least $\int_0^{\|z_0\|}du/\omega(u)$; arrival is impossible whenever this integral diverges, and when it is finite it is the exact threshold, attained inside the class. The classical settling expressions of finite-time control reappear as hitting-time floors, and the known fixed-time condition is the two-ended convergence of the same integral. For linear time-varying loops the results refine to logarithmic-norm budgets, corollaries of a known two-sided estimate, with the terminal error of gain freezing described exactly.
item.dc:creator: Osama F. Abdel Aal, Jiale Chen, Jairo Viola, YangQuan Chen

item.title: Covariance-Rank Rounding and a Sharp Integrality Gap for a Matroid Edge-Coverage Moment Lift
item.description: arXiv:2610.17512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Selecting vertices covers their incident edges, but a matroid can prevent selecting the combinations that cover the most weight. We study whether pair-selection information improves rounding from a semidefinite relaxation of this problem. A feasible point $(x,Y)$ records individual and paired selection values. Its relaxation objective is $U$, and the matrix $Y-xx^\top$ has rank $d$. We compare the feasible marginal vectors obtained by fixing one element as selected or excluded, then round only the best vector. For $d\ge1$, the resulting basis has value at least $(3/4+1/(4d))U$. The procedure is deterministic and polynomial-time for a supplied exact rational point and an independence oracle. Weighting the covariance spectrum by the objective gives a stronger version of the bound. To show the rank factor is sharp, we construct a rank-$2m$ rational linear matroid and $m$ disjoint four-cycles with integral optimum $3m+1$, relaxation optimum $4m$, and an optimal covariance matrix of rank $m$. Thus the relaxation has limiting reciprocal integrality gap $4/3$, despite its conditional constraints. One valid pair-exclusion inequality makes it exact on this family, as an explicit semidefinite certificate shows. The result concerns rounding and the strength of this relaxation; it does not supply a low-rank optimal point or a fixed universal approximation improvement.
item.dc:creator: Navid Rezazadeh

item.title: Matroid-Aware Spectral Certificates for Multiplicative Coverage Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.17514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We maximize the weight of edges covered by selected vertices, together with nonnegative individual rewards, under an arbitrary matroid constraint. The continuous coverage objective is quadratic and need not be concave. Our method searches projections onto a small set of directions and solves a concave subproblem for each projection center. A coverage-specific inequality converts the subproblem bounds into a multiplicative guarantee, while matroid rounding restores an integral solution. Let $A$ be the weighted adjacency matrix and $D$ the diagonal matrix of singleton values, restricted to positive-value elements after objective-preserving preprocessing. Set $\varrho=\lambda_{\max}(D^{-1/2}AD^{-1/2})$. For an integer budget $q\ge0$, let $\tau_q$ be the smallest nonnegative threshold for which $A+\tau_qD$ has at most $q$ negative eigenvalues on the span of differences of matroid bases. We obtain the factor $1-\varrho\tau_q/[2(\varrho+\tau_q)]-\varepsilon$ in time $(2+q/\varepsilon)^{O(q+1)}N^{O(1)}$, where $N$ is the binary input length and a zero-over-zero loss is zero. The algorithm returns a rational upper bound on the integral optimum. A separate exact-algebraic construction produces polynomial-bit low-rank rational corrections with positive threshold slack; its proof isolates eigenvalues, keeps eigenspace bases unnormalized, and approximates scalar factors only at the final step. The numerical proposal prototype is not used to justify this complexity statement. Supplied certificates also yield robustness to locally bounded edge additions. These are threshold-dependent coverage guarantees, not a new general spectral-search principle or a universal approximation improvement.
item.dc:creator: Navid Rezazadeh

item.title: Sharp Damping Location for Stability of a Locally Damped Wave Equation and its Galerkin Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.17539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the stability of the variable coefficient wave equation $u_{tt}-u_{xx}-(1+x^{2})u_{yy}+\chi_{\mathbb G}u_{t}=0$ on the rectangle $(-1,1)\times(0,\pi)$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions, where the viscous damping acts on a vertical strip $\mathbb G=(\eta-\delta,\eta+\delta)\times(0,\pi)$. We establish a precise relationship between the location of the damping region and the rate of energy decay. We prove that the associated semigroup is exponentially stable whenever the closure of the damping strip meets the line $x=0$, i.e., $|\eta|\leq\delta$, despite the existence of rays that never enter the damped region. When the damping region is strictly bounded away from $x=0$, the semigroup decays at the sharp rate $(\log(2+t))^{-1}$. The proofs combine separation of variables, one-dimensional resolvent estimates, a reflection identity for the harmonic oscillator, and Gaussian quasimodes. We then consider the spectral Galerkin approximation based on the Dirichlet eigenfunctions of the constant coefficient Laplacian and show that, although the sequence of semigroups resulting from the approximation converges to the continuous one, it fails to be uniformly exponentially stable.
item.dc:creator: Kangsheng Liu, Lihui Lu, Qiong Zhang

item.title: Convex-Analytic View of Query Selection for Safety Verification of Markov Decision Processes
item.description: arXiv:2610.17541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety verification of a Markov decision process (MDP) asks whether the probabilities of reaching several failure states jointly lie in a convex safe region under every scheduler. Watanabe and Unno (2026) prove safety by refining an outer approximation of the failure probabilities, where each query bounds a nonnegative weighted sum of the probabilities. Their rule selects weights by the largest Euclidean violation. We present a unified framework to measure violation in an explicitly chosen error unit: directions are scored by the support-function gap between the outer approximation and the safe region, normalized by the support function of the unit. We show that the maximal score, when positive, equals the smallest enlargement of the safe region in multiples of that unit that contains the outer approximation. The Euclidean unit recovers the earlier rule; two new rules are generated by the unit cube and the safe region itself. We experimentally evaluate how the choice of measurement rule affects the performance of safety verification for MDPs.
item.dc:creator: Han Bao, Shinsaku Sakaue, Kazuki Watanabe

item.title: Boundary Control of a Modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest Beam via Reduced-Order Reinforcement Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.17563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the active vibration control of an elastic beam using reinforcement learning (RL). The physical system is modeled by a modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest type linear partial differential equation with simply supported boundary conditions. The dynamics are approximated by a reduced-order model (ROM) obtained through eigenvalue expansion and truncated Galerkin projection. Control is applied through boundary actuation. The resulting finite-dimensional system is formulated as a continuous-time Markov decision process and solved numerically using the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm. All modeling steps, from physical formulation to temporal discretization and control design, are explicitly described. A systematic comparison is performed between the controller learned via PPO and the classical linear quadratic (LQR) regulator. The analysis highlights the strengths and limitations of each approach, both from a theoretical and practical point of view, with particular emphasis on energy dissipation mechanisms and actuator constraints.
item.dc:creator: Leonardo R S Rodrigues

item.title: Optimal transportation under McKean-Vlasov dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.17626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a broad class of stochastic transport problems under controlled McKean-Vlasov dynamics, allowing control of both drift and volatility, with weak terminal constraints. In contrast to the classical Schr\"odinger problem, the reference dynamics depend on the evolving law of the process, leading to nonlinear optimization problems on path space, while the terminal constraint is formulated through weak optimal transport, permitting a flexible treatment of distributional targets. This framework encompasses several problems of current interest, including the mean field Schr\"odinger problem, martingale optimal transport, and Schr\"odinger-Bass bridges. We establish three main results. First, we prove the existence of optimal controls under general coercivity, continuity, and convexity assumptions. Second, we derive a convex dual representation that extends weak Kantorovich duality and stochastic optimal transport duality to controlled McKean-Vlasov dynamics. Finally, for the mean field Schr\"odinger problem, we prove convergence, at the level of value functions, of the associated finite-particle Schr\"odinger bridge problems to the mean field limit, thereby identifying the nonlinear problem as the exact infinite-particle limit of finite-particle Schr\"odinger bridges. As a byproduct, we establish the existence of an optimal mean field Schr\"odinger potential, providing a variational foundation for duality in nonlinear stochastic transport.
item.dc:creator: Camilo Hern\'andez, Ludovic Tangpi

item.title: H-PDLP: GPU-Accelerated Linear Programming via Generalized PDHG and Homogeneous Self-Dual Embedding
item.description: arXiv:2610.17695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GPU-based first-order methods are emerging as an approach for solving large-scale linear programming (LP) problems. We present H-PDLP, a GPU first-order LP solver based on a generalized primal-dual hybrid gradient (PDHG) method for a homogeneous self-dual embedding of the LP, and study its numerical performance. The solver applies the restarted reflected Halpern iteration to the generalized PDHG operator, with the embedding encoding both primal-dual optimal solutions and certificates of primal or dual infeasibility. We derive a compact embedding for LPs with two-sided constraint and variable bounds in which the bounds enter through box cones, and we show that the resulting box-cone projections reduce to one-dimensional root-finding problems, so that each iteration remains matrix-free and well suited to GPUs. On the theoretical side, we establish conditions under which the iterates remain uniformly bounded away from the trivial zero solution of the embedding and derive complexity guarantees for the method. We also introduce MIPLIBInfeas, a reproducible benchmark of 229 infeasible and 105 unbounded LPs derived from MIPLIB 2017. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach on both feasible LPs and infeasible or unbounded LPs. The source code for H-PDLP is publicly available at https://github.com/MIT-Lu-Lab/H-PDLP.
item.dc:creator: Haihao Lu, Bo Tang

item.title: Portfolio Selection by Joint Estimation-Robustness Optimization with the Return and Risk Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.17756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In answering the main criticism of the classical robust optimization that the size of the uncertainty set has to be determined beforehand, a recently proposed Joint Estimation and Robustness Optimization framework treats the size of the uncertainty set as a variable and maximizes it subject to some robust conditions over the uncertainty set. This paper studies its effect on portfolio selection when both the robust return and risk constraints are built into Joint Estimation and Robustness Optimization framework. Although this framework does not directly pursuit any optimality of portfolio return or risk, we report a surprising result that Joint Estimation and Robustness Optimization framework actually selects efficient portfolios. This is proved by reformulating the robust risk constraint as a tractable form through the S-procedure. Moreover, a closed-form formula was derived when there is only the budget constraint. An efficient algorithm is proposed when more constraints are added. Numerical experiments illustrate the validity of the reported results. This research paves the way for Joint Estimation and Robustness Optimization framework to be applied to the portfolio selection problem with return and risk related robust constraints.
item.dc:creator: Yingxiao Wang, Lingchen Kong, Selin D. Ahipasaoglu, Houduo Qi

item.title: Minimal norm control problems for linear mean-field control systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.17825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies controllability and minimal norm control problems (NP problems) for mean-field stochastic differential equation (MF-SDE) systems. We first establish an equivalent rank criterion for terminal controllability, namely, that the diffusion matrices $D$ and $D+\bar D$ are both of full row rank. We then derive an explicit Riccati-based representation of the minimal norm control by applying a parameterization technique. A key step is to identify the value $P(0)$ of an associated Riccati solution with the controllability Gramian of a controllable auxiliary system, which yields the parameter required in the construction. The resulting representation provides a basis for the future development and analysis of numerical methods for NP problems.
item.dc:creator: Manfen An, Rui Gao, Yanqing Wang

item.title: Theoretical and Computational Advances in Birkhoff Pseudospectral Transcription for Aerospace Optimal Control
item.description: arXiv:2610.17842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops theoretical and numerical extensions of Birkhoff pseudospectral transcription for aerospace optimal control problems. Building on the recently proposed body of knowledge, a Birkhoff integration operator is derived for flipped Legendre Gauss Radau (fLGR) grids, drawing connections to regular LGR grids and to the favorable conditioning properties that make Birkhoff interpolants particularly appealing. We also propose the enforcement of differential constraints via pseudospectral operators, and the primal and dual equivalence of this approach to state augmentation is established for control-rate limits. The numerical developments include the formulation and solution of heterogeneous multiphase optimal control problems, parameterized non-affine time mappings, composition of affine scaling and equilibration methods, and a hybrid derivative strategy to combine linear pseudospectral operators with numerical derivatives for nonlinear functions. These methods are implemented in the RAPTOR (Rapid Algorithm for Pseudospectral Trajectory Optimization and Robustification) transcription framework and assessed through feature-oriented benchmarks: a one-dimensional landing problem, a planar orbit-raising scenario, an atmospheric entry problem, and a multiphase reusable launch vehicle problem with simultaneous booster-recovery and upper-stage-insertion trajectories.
item.dc:creator: Riccardo Minnozzi, Marco Sagliano

item.title: Non-Contiguous Channel Allocation in Multi-Beam Satellites: Formulations, Upper Bounds and Cooperative Matheuristics
item.description: arXiv:2610.17906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Demand for wireless communication is growing, and commercial satellite services are expanding with it, increasing pressure on a finite radio spectrum. Allocation efficiency directly limits how many users a satellite can serve. We study how to assign frequency sub-channels to the carriers of a multi-beam satellite, maximising the total priority of admitted carriers while keeping each within its interference tolerance. Earlier work on this interference-limited channel allocation problem placed each carrier in a single continuous frequency block. Removing this restriction can admit more carriers, but a direct integer programming model cannot solve the largest test problems in practical time, so new methods are needed. We prove the problem computationally hard, reformulate it around how carriers share sub-channels, and derive three bounds on the optimum. We develop heuristics, including matheuristics combining local search with optimisation models, and an orchestrated portfolio that schedules them, recombines their solutions and stops early once its result is proven optimal or no longer improves. On 24 problems with up to 500 carriers, the best heuristics come within about 1% of the best known solution on average. The portfolio matches or exceeds the best heuristic for each problem on 23 of 24 with equal weights and 22 with priority weights, and is up to about 5% better on larger, more congested problems. It requires about a quarter of the time to run every heuristic and keep the best, and under half that of its heuristics run in a fixed order, which return slightly worse solutions on average.
item.dc:creator: Angus Gaudry, Vicky Mak-Hau

item.title: On integrability of local utility maximizing strategies
item.description: arXiv:2610.17915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In stochastic control problems involving optimal portfolio choice, one often seeks an optimizer of some local criterion (dynamic programming value function) generated by some global criterion (e.g., expected utility). The local optimizer then typically acts as a stochastic integrand with respect to some multivariate stochastic process (e.g., asset prices). This paper takes a closer look at local criteria in the form of ``local expected utility''. Since the existence of the local optimizer can be established under very mild conditions, it is crucial to understand under what circumstances the local optimizer has good integrability properties. It is shown that the reasonable asymptotic elasticity condition of Kramkov and Schachermayer (1999) applied to the local utility function plays a key role in this context.
item.dc:creator: Ale\v{s} \v{C}ern\'{y}, Johannes Ruf

item.title: Control Realization of Schr\"{o}dinger Bridges over Discrete-Time Nonlinear Systems via Maximum-Entropy Distribution Steering
item.description: arXiv:2610.17965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper shows how a Schrodinger bridge (SB) structure emerges from maximum-entropy (MaxEnt) distribution steering of discrete-time nonlinear systems. We also establish that the resulting bridge can be realized by an optimal control policy. We consider general state and input costs, non-Gaussian endpoint distributions, and input constraints. Assuming the existence of a feasible policy with finite objective value, we show that the state-path measure under a MaxEnt optimal control policy is the unique SB. The reference measure of this SB is induced by an optimal policy of the corresponding terminal-unconstrained problem. Moreover, we give an equivalent characterization of the optimal state-path measure using a killed reference and its normalized Feynman--Kac measure, thereby interpreting the state cost as killing. We then characterize the finite-cost feasibility by the existence of an endpoint coupling having finite Kullback--Leibler divergence from the reference endpoint distribution. For compactly supported marginals with bounded target density, we derive reachability-based sufficient conditions guaranteeing this feasibility. We further provide specializations to fully actuated control-affine and reachable linear systems.
item.dc:creator: Kaito Ito, Kenji Kashima

item.title: Optimal Control of Mean-field FBSDEs and Classical Solutions of the Related Generalized HJB Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.18015v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we study optimal control problems driven by mean-field forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs). The aim is two-fold: (i) to provide the unique optimal control; (ii) to establish classical solutions of the associated generalized Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations on the space of probability measures. For (i), we study the coupled system arising from the maximum principle, which involves both the state FBSDEs and the adjoint FBSDEs. This system is non-standard and more complicated than that in standard mean-field type control (MFTC) problems. By extending the method of continuation in the coefficients to our framework, we establish the well-posedness result, and subsequently obtain the differentiability of the value functional with respect to the distribution argument --- thereby extending existing results for MFTC problems. For (ii), since the flow property does not generally hold for control problems of FBSDEs, standard dynamic-programming arguments cannot be applied directly. We therefore develop probabilistic approaches to the classical solvability of generalized HJB equations under three distinct sets of conditions. The auxiliary processes arising in these arguments differ significantly from those in standard MFTC problems. We establish new connections between the value function and the adjoint processes, derive equations for the relevant decoupling field, and obtain first- and second-order generalized HJB equations, including a coupled system on the space of probability measures. The standard HJB equations for MFTC problems are recovered as special cases. Our approach yields classical solutions without requiring non-degeneracy of the diffusion.
item.dc:creator: Ziyu Huang

item.title: Lifted Restricted Isometry Property and Fast Algorithm for Spectral Compressed Sensing With Near-Optimal Sample Complexity
item.description: arXiv:2610.18032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the spectral compressed sensing problem, which aims to recover an $r$-spectrally-sparse signal of length $N$ from linear compressive measurements. We reformulate the problem as the recovery of a low-rank Hankel matrix. Motivated by this formulation, we propose a Lifted Restricted Isometry Property (LRIP) for the measurement matrix and show that Gaussian measurement matrices satisfy LRIP under certain conditions. Unlike classical RIP, LRIP imposes a rank constraint in the lifted matrix domain while taking measurements in the signal domain through the adjoint Hankel operator. To solve the resulting nonconvex problem efficiently, we introduce a Fast Iterative Hard Thresholding (FIHT) algorithm. Based on LRIP, we show that FIHT converges linearly to the true signal with high probability using $\mathcal{O}(r \ln r \ln^2 N)$ scaled Gaussian measurements, which is near-optimal up to log factors and improves the state-of-the-art order of $r^2$ for nonconvex Hankel methods. Extensive numerical results demonstrate the superiority of FIHT as compared to state-of-the-art convex methods in terms of phase transitions, computational time, and robustness to noise.
item.dc:creator: Xunmeng Wu, Jian-Feng Cai, Zongben Xu, Zai Yang

item.title: Non-Potential Congestion Games with a Continuum of Players
item.description: arXiv:2610.18035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a class of congestion games with a continuum of heterogeneous players and a finite set of resources, without assuming the existence of a potential function. Players differ in their individual characteristics and may contribute differently to congestion, which is represented through general aggregate features of the population choosing each resource. We characterize the conditions under which such a game admits a potential and show that this structure generally fails when players have heterogeneous impacts on congestion. To analyze the non-potential case, we introduce the concept of Stochastic Variational Nash Equilibrium, in which players observe idiosyncratic cost shocks before selecting a resource. We show that equilibrium choices are pure conditional on players' characteristics and shock realizations, whereas the induced aggregate allocation is probabilistic. Under Gumbel-distributed shocks, the equilibrium is equivalent to a continuum-player logit Quantal Response Equilibrium. Using a fixed-point formulation and the Schauder--Tychonoff theorem, we establish existence for every positive noise level and recover a pure Nash equilibrium in the zero-noise limit. Under a coordinate-wise monotonicity condition on aggregate interaction costs, we further prove uniqueness and convergence of the regularized allocations to the pure equilibrium. An application to electric vehicle charging illustrates how heterogeneous energy demands jointly affect station choice, congestion, and market shares.
item.dc:creator: Alix Dupont, Quentin Petit, Adrien S\'eguret

item.title: A Smoothed Augmented Lagrangian Method for Mathematical Programs with Vertical Complementarity Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.18048v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a smoothed augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) for solving mathematical programs with vertical complementarity constraints (VCCs). The augmented Lagrangian function involving the VCCs is smoothed by the Lasry--Lions double envelope, which is an extension of the Moreau envelope that enjoys enhanced smoothness properties. This construction yields a smooth unconstrained subproblem within the ALM framework that can be efficiently solved by many fast optimization algorithms. In the limiting setting, we establish global convergence to Mordukhovich- and Clarke-stationary points. For the convergence rate, we show that, under appropriate assumptions, the smoothed ALM achieves Q-linear convergence. We further provide a worst-case iteration complexity analysis for computing an approximate stationary point of the original problem or of an associated feasibility problem. Preliminary numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
item.dc:creator: Jia Wang, Andreas Themelis, Panagiotis Patrinos

item.title: UQ-ACE: Stability-Aware Counterfactual Controller Tuning via Bayesian SINDy
item.description: arXiv:2610.18156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retuning feedback controllers in critical processes is challenging when experiments are costly, open-loop excitation is infeasible, and candidate controllers must be screened before deployment. The existing Adaptive Sampling for Counterfactual Explanations (ACE) method provides a sample-efficient approach for finding minimal controller-parameter changes that recover prescribed closed-loop performance, but it does not explicitly account for stability of candidate controllers proposed during the search, which may be destabilizing under plant uncertainty. This paper introduces UQ-ACE, a stability-aware retuning method based on Bayesian SINDy. In UQ-ACE, closed-loop trajectories are used to infer a posterior distribution over local dynamical models, from which candidate controllers are screened for stability before implementation. Extensive simulations show that UQ-ACE achieves valid retunings with few closed-loop experiments while preventing deployment of unstable candidates.
item.dc:creator: Margarita A. Guerrero, Rodrigo A. Gonzalez, Cristian R. Rojas

item.title: Composite and Stochastic Smoothed Decentralized Bregman Proximal-Gradient Methods
item.description: arXiv:2610.18231v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Smoothed decentralized Bregman proximal-gradient (SDBPG) methods combine relative-smoothness geometry with edge-dual consensus. We extend SDBPG to node-specific convex nonsmooth regularizers and unbiased stochastic local gradients while retaining its Bregman primal-dual smoothing mechanism. The analysis isolates temporal subgradient motion and aggregation mismatch as two defect sequences. For trajectories in a forward-invariant compact subset of the kernel domain and admissible parameters, finite accumulated defects yield an $O(T^{-1})$ bound on the squared best-iterate proximal residual over $T$ iterations. The stochastic bound separates accumulated oracle variance from expected defects and attains the same order when the variance bounds and expected defects are summable. Common active-structure identification, together with local subgradient conditions, gives sufficient finite-defect conditions for $\ell_1$ and group $\ell_{2,1}$ regularization. Experiments with common regularizers and heterogeneous sensing operators relate defect decay to observed support stabilization and compare reconstruction and communication with decentralized proximal and gradient-tracking methods. A separate phase-retrieval study evaluates the effect of a quartic Bregman kernel. Code and experiment scripts are available at https://github.com/shengze-xu/composite-stochastic-sdbpg .
item.dc:creator: Shengze Xu, Chenhan Jin, Qingsong Wang, Tieyong Zeng

item.title: Improved Analysis of Adaptive Task Allocation and Non-Stationary Processing Times
item.description: arXiv:2610.18265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the task allocation problem, where our goal is to develop an online algorithm that efficiently distributes tasks among workers based on their computational performance. This task is challenging since computation times are random and non-stationary in practice. Recent works have introduced different online algorithms to address this problem. One of them is Adaptive Task Allocation (ATA), a bandit-style algorithm. However, previous theoretical guarantees leave substantial room for improvement, and existing methods are designed only for stationary computation times. Using new proof techniques, our work establishes an improved analysis of ATA with better gap-dependent and gap-independent regret guarantees, improving upon all previous approaches. We also introduce a new method, Sliding Window Adaptive Task Allocation (SW-ATA), designed for more practical non-stationary environments. Finally, we prove new lower bounds in both the stationary and non-stationary settings.
item.dc:creator: Grigory Begunov, Ilgam Latypov, Yuriy Dorn, Alexander Tyurin

item.title: A Projection Anderson Acceleration Algorithm for Non-quasi-monotone Variational Inequalities with H\"older Continuous Terms
item.description: arXiv:2610.18370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a Projection Anderson Acceleration (PAA) algorithm for variational inequality (VI) problems, where the underlying function is expressed as a finite sum of H\"older continuous functions and satisfies the $\sigma$-star strongly monotone condition that includes the star strong monotonicity with $\sigma = 1$ as a special case. In the absence of quasi-monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity, we establish the evaluation complexity of the PAA algorithm for finding an approximate solution. Specifically, for the star strongly monotone VI problems, the PAA algorithm needs at most $O (\log (\epsilon^{-1}) \epsilon^{2 (\underline{\alpha} - 1)})$ evaluations of the function and projection for finding an $\epsilon$-approximate solution, where $\underline{\alpha} \in (0, 1]$ is the smallest exponent of H{\"o}lder continuity of the component functions. We illustrate our theoretical results by numerical examples of non-quasi-monotone complementarity problems and non-monotone semilinear elliptic equations with non-Lipschitz terms.
item.dc:creator: Xiaojun Chen, C. T. Kelley, Lei Wang

item.title: Quantitative Convergence of Markov Equilibria for Time-Inconsistent Controlled Diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2610.18376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-inconsistent stochastic control admits a natural game-theoretic interpretation in which successive decision dates are represented by different selves. In the Markovian framework of Bj\"ork-Khapko-Murgoci, the corresponding continuous-time equilibrium HJB system can be motivated by discrete subgame-perfect games, but the general discrete-to-continuous passage is not automatic. We establish a quantitative convergence theorem for a smooth uniformly elliptic class in which the control may enter both drift and diffusion. Using the exact sample-and-hold transition law on each time step, we construct, near a verified continuous equilibrium branch, a unique regular discrete Markov subgame-perfect equilibrium and prove first-order convergence of the continuation objects in an anisotropic $C^{2+\beta}$ topology and of the equilibrium policies in $C^0$. The key stability mechanism is structural: the discrete first-order condition forces the differential feedback correction in the frozen linearization to be nilpotent, which yields mesh-uniform block estimates through a two-norm dyadic Schauder argument despite the second-order coupling caused by controlled volatility. We also formulate a conditional transfer principle for structured polynomial-growth classes, with error-space stability stated as a separate hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Sascha Desmettre

item.title: Optimal Transport for Continuous-Time Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection
item.description: arXiv:2610.18398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The continuous-time mean-variance portfolio selection problem is investigated in this paper through a rigorous integration of backward stochastic differential equation (BSDE) and Kantorovich duality theory. We propose a novel analytical framework for addressing feedback control in McKean-Vlasov stochastic systems. By solving three coupled systems of ordinary differential equations (ODEs), we derive an explicit, closed-loop optimal feedback investment strategy.
item.dc:creator: Yijie Zeng, Liangquan Zhang, Xun Li

item.title: Adaptive Variance-Reduced Stochastic Sequential (Quadratic Constrained) Quadratic Programming
item.description: arXiv:2610.18428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose an adaptive variance-reduced stochastic sequential (quadratic constrained) quadratic programming (AVR-SS(QC)QP) method for nonlinear constrained optimization. The framework integrates SPIDER-based variance reduction, stochastic quasi-Newton curvature information, merit-function globalization, and adaptive switching between stochastic SQP and SQCQP models. The switching mechanism is governed by a relative constraint model curvature indicator that measures the second-order constraint information neglected by the linearized SQP model. A smoothed hysteresis rule ac?tivates the SQCQP model only when the relative constraint curvature is significant. An exact L1 merit function with Armijo backtracking globalizes the resulting directions, while a coupled stochastic Lyapunov analysis controls the interaction between gradient-estimation error and optimization progress. Under standard smoothness, sampling, regularity, and second-order conditions, we establish almost-sure consistency of the variance-reduced gradient estimator and global convergence of the KKT residual. We further show that, near regular KKT points, the curvature indicator vanishes and the method eventually selects the computationally cheaper SQP model. Numerical experiments on a sparse principal component analysis problem illustrate the practical be?havior of the proposed framework.
item.dc:creator: Gopal Tiwari, Md Abu Talhamainuddin Ansary

item.title: Connection between MP and DPP for Mean-Field Stochastic Optimal Control Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.18437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper deals with the optimal control problem for the general mean-field stochastic differential equations, in which the coefficients depend on both the state process as well as on its law. We focus on the connection between the general maximum principle and the dynamic programming principle for such a control problem. We establish the relationship between the value function of the mean-field optimal control problem and the adjoint equations in the maximum principle. We also give a general mean-field stochastic verification theorem. Some examples are solved explicitly to illustrate our results.
item.dc:creator: Guangzhi Cui, Tianyang Nie, Guangchen Wang

item.title: Hamiltonian Primal-Dual Policy Reinforcement Learning for Derivative-Free Model-Based Control
item.description: arXiv:2610.18524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite-horizon optimal control becomes difficult when a dynamical model can be simulated reliably, but its derivatives are unavailable, discontinuous, or unreliable. Hamiltonian Primal-Dual Policy Optimization (HPDPO) is introduced as a derivative-free, model-based reinforcement learning framework for this setting. The control is represented as a time-indexed finite-horizon policy. Candidate actions are evaluated by deterministic suffix rollouts of the supplied transition model, while a regularized Hamiltonian dual formulation supplies structured future-cost information through block-coordinate multiplier updates. No differentiation of the state dynamics or learned critic is required. The method is validated on nonsmooth problems with exact solutions, an analytical and learned ReLU biomarker cascade, an amyloid Neural ODE trained from longitudinal ADNI data, and three multidimensional-control problems with up to five simultaneous controls. Across these examples, HPDPO closely reproduces exact or reference objective values, trajectories, and control structures. The results show that forward simulation and Hamiltonian dual structure can be combined to solve deterministic finite-horizon control problems involving nonsmooth, learned, or black-box dynamics.
item.dc:creator: K. Rabiei, Z. Rui, X. Lu, W. Hao

item.title: Local-discrepancy ambiguity sets for distributionally robust optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.18590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new class of data-driven ambiguity sets for distributionally robust optimization (DRO) that aim to enhance the local inference accuracy of an unknown distribution. Building on optimal transport-based discrepancy measures, we depart from the conventional paradigm of monolithic ambiguity balls, which rely on a single global transport budget to capture distributional uncertainty. Instead, we introduce local-discrepancy ambiguity sets, where the support of the distribution is partitioned into predefined regions and transport cost constraints are imposed locally to each region. This added flexibility allows for a more refined characterization of plausible distributions by preventing highly imbalanced transport across regions. As a result, the proposed approach can yield less conservative and more robust decisions, particularly in settings where decisions depend on the local properties of the sample space. We further derive tractable reformulations of the resulting DRO problems and demonstrate through simulations that our method can outperform traditional Wasserstein ambiguity sets in terms of decision quality.
item.dc:creator: Ilias Papagoudis, Dimitris Boskos

item.title: Dynamic Programming for A Linear-Gaussian Dual Control Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.18630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider an infinite-horizon discounted dynamic programming (DP) problem for a countable-innovation belief-state model. The model is a surrogate for a linear-Gaussian dual control problem involving an unknown parameter vector and Gaussian observation noise. The surrogate preserves the first two moments of the Gaussian innovation and the resulting posterior second-moment structure. We allow unbounded belief and control spaces and nonnegative stage costs with quadratic growth in the posterior mean and covariance. Using a posterior-moment weight, we show that the Bellman operator is a contraction in a weighted sup-norm space. We characterize the optimal cost as the unique solution of the Bellman equation in this space, establish the existence of optimal stationary policies. We further prove weighted sup-norm convergence of value iteration, policy iteration, and optimistic policy iteration under vanishing approximation errors. The convergence results under vanishing approximation errors rely on general weighted sup-norm contraction properties and are applicable beyond the particular dual control problem considered here.
item.dc:creator: Ying Wang, Yuchao Li, H{\aa}kan Hjalmarsson

item.title: Optimal Decay Matrix Control Barrier Functions: Soundness and Completeness for Matrix Safety Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.18675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many safety requirements, such as keeping a manipulator away from kinematic singularities, a network connected, or a system observable, amount to keeping a state-dependent matrix positive definite. Matrix control barrier functions (MCBFs) enforce such requirements with a semidefinite program that minimally modifies a nominal control input. The MCBF constraint bounds how fast the safety margin, the smallest eigenvalue of the matrix, may decay. Yet a fixed decay rule is conservative, rejecting safe controls that drive the state quickly toward, but never across, the boundary of the safe set. Scalar optimal decay (SOD) addresses this issue by scaling the decay term by a scalar weight that is optimized together with the control. For scalar barrier functions, SOD then rejects a control at the boundary only if the control would decrease the margin. For MCBFs, however, SOD can reject controls that leave the margin unchanged, and near the safety boundary SOD accepts such controls only at a high cost. We introduce matrix optimal decay (MOD), which replaces the scalar weight with a matrix multiplier while keeping the semidefinite program convex. MOD is provably sound and complete, certifying at the boundary exactly the controls that do not decrease the margin. If some control can strictly increase the margin at every boundary point, the MOD-MCBF filtered controller is continuous and renders the safe set forward invariant. We also add an optional recovery condition that drives the system toward the safe set after a violation without affecting soundness or completeness. On a planar two-link arm avoiding singularities, MOD-MCBF certifies safe motions that both a fixed decay rule and SOD reject, and tracks an end-effector target more closely than SOD.
item.dc:creator: Samuel G. Gessow, Albert Wu, Aaron D. Ames, Brett T. Lopez

item.title: Compositional Sensitivity Analysis for Multiobjective System Co-Design
item.description: arXiv:2610.18758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sensitivity analysis of coupled systems typically propagates derivatives of single-valued maps, whereas multiobjective optimization generally treats sensitivity at the system level rather than through interconnected subsystems. We develop a mathematical framework for compositional sensitivity analysis in multiobjective system design, building on monotone co-design. Subsystems are represented as design problems (DPs), interconnected through series, parallel, union, intersection, and feedback composition. We introduce tangential DPs (TDPs) to describe first-order variations around an operating point, show that they preserve the structure of DPs, and characterize their queries through graphical derivatives. To account for multiple internal realizations of a system-level operating point, tangential co-design problems compose families of local TDPs by taking a union over these realizations while retaining the original interconnection structure. We show that these compositions yield families of TDPs and establish conditions under which sensitivity analysis commutes with individual composition operations. Beyond infinitesimal sensitivity, we show that bounded tangential models of convex DPs provide tighter outer approximations of feasible finite changes, which can be propagated through co-design problems without union compositions. We conclude with several convex and nonconvex numerical examples that showcase the framework's accuracy and computational benefits.
item.dc:creator: Alan Bonomi, Antonio Terpin, Yubo Cai, Yujun Huang, Meshal Alharbi, Gioele Zardini

item.title: Platonic geodesic trees in the $K-$Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.13950v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, We prove that: (A) If $m\ge 4,$ there exists a Platonic geodesic tree having $m$ edges (geodesic segments), which form $m$ platonic angles with measure $120^{o}$ and $(\frac{m(m-1)}{2}-m)$ platonic angles with measure $90^{o}.$ (Existence of a Fermat Coordinate system) (B) If $m=2,$ there exists a Platonic geodesic tree with three vertices and 2 edges, which meet at $120^{\circ}$ or $150^{\circ}$ or $180^{\circ}$ (Minimal spanning geodesic tree). (C) If $m=3,$ there exists a Platonic tree and the Steiner point is identical with the Fermat point, having three edges, which meet at $120^{\circ}$ (Hexagonal coordinate system). (D) If $m$ is even and $m \ge 4,$ there exists a Platonic geodesic tree having $m$ edges , which form platonic angles with only two distinct measures $90^{o}$ and $180^{\circ}.$ (Existence of a Cartesian coordinate system). (E) If $m\ge 4$, there does not exist a Platonic geodesic tree having $m$ edges , which form only platonic angles with measure $120^{o}$ (Non existence of a Fermat coordinate system). (F) If $m\ge 3,$ there does not exist a Platonic geodesic tree having $m$ edges, which form platonic angles with only one measure $150^{o},$ or two distinct measures $120^{\circ}$ and $150^{\circ}$ or two distinct measures $90^{\circ}$ and $150^{\circ}$ (Non existence of a Fermat coordinate system). A classification of platonic geodesic trees with boundary vertex set $V$ and added vertex set $Q$ in the $K-$Space is given by conditions (A), (B), (C), (D), (E), (F), which characterize each vertex in $V\cup Q.$
item.dc:creator: Anastasios N. Zachos

item.title: Generalized PINN-Based Inverse Estimation of Spatially Varying Heat Transfer Coefficients with Transfer Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.14008v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This study investigates generalized boundary representations and transfer learning for physics-informed neural-network (PINN) estimation of spatially varying convective heat transfer coefficients (HTCs) in jet impingement cooling. Piecewise-linear (PWL) and neural-network boundary estimators are inferred from transient interior-temperature measurements and evaluated against CFD-CHT reference HTC profiles at Reynolds numbers of 5000, 10000 and 15000. A discrete Adjoint-FEM formulation with gradient regularization based on the $H^1$-seminorm provides an independent inverse-method comparison. Transfer learning is investigated under two source-target conditions: transfer between noise levels at the same Reynolds number, and transfer from a controlled Gaussian-profile problem to CFD-CHT-derived target problems at different Reynolds numbers. For the representative Re = 5000 target with 5% measurement noise, quadratic, PWL, and neural-network PINNs achieve relative HTC-profile errors of 5.08, 5.31 and 5.19%, respectively, while generalized representations reduce the error for the Re = 15000 target from 16.76% for the quadratic PINN to 14.41% and 14.46%. Transfer learning reduces target-training time by 57.86-81.71% for fixed-Reynolds-number transfer and by 50.59-84.94% for Gaussian-to-CHT transfer. Its effect on reconstruction accuracy is target dependent: fixed-profile PWL transfer remains within 0.30 percentage points of scratch training, whereas Gaussian-to-CHT transfer produces differences of 0.10-1.52 percentage points across targets and representations. These results demonstrate that generalized PINN representations can accommodate spatially varying HTC profiles without a prescribed quadratic form, while transfer learning can substantially reduce target-training cost for repeated inverse estimation, with the resulting reconstruction accuracy depending on source-target compatibility.
item.dc:creator: Pradipan Maitra, Jariful Hassan, Arijit Hazra

item.title: Zero-Crossing Time Lower Bounds for the Homogeneous Super-Twisting Algorithm
item.description: arXiv:2610.14285v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: High-frequency switching and chattering are well-known problems in sliding-mode control. Although the super-twisting algorithm produces a continuous control input, the sliding variable may still cross zero repeatedly near the sliding manifold. This paper studies how fast these crossings can occur and whether they can accumulate in finite time for the scalar homogeneous super-twisting algorithm. Two lower bounds on the time required to return to zero are derived, together with a bound on the time needed to complete a full excursion. These results give minimum separation times and upper bounds on the number of crossings associated with excursions above a prescribed amplitude. Although zero crossings may accumulate in finite time, the amplitudes of the complete excursions considered here must vanish and satisfy a summability condition. Thus, crossings associated with excursions above any prescribed nonzero amplitude cannot accumulate in finite time. When the perturbation-rate bound is zero, the estimates recover the scaling imposed by homogeneity. For the classical super-twisting algorithm, the square-root scaling also holds for nonzero perturbation-rate bounds. Numerical simulations illustrate the results.
item.dc:creator: Diego Guti\'errez-Oribio, Ioannis Stefanou

item.title: Decentralized Bandit Learning of Markov Perfect Equilibria
item.description: arXiv:2610.14333v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study decentralized bandit learning in discounted infinite-horizon, general-sum Markov games with continuous actions. Agents observe the public state, but only their own realized rewards, and use simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation to update their actions. Under strong monotonicity of the negative running-reward gradients and sufficiently small time steps, we prove that the fully decentralized procedure converges almost surely to the unique stationary Markov perfect equilibrium. We obtain an $O(n^{-1/2})$ convergence rate and present a natural extension to episodic finite-horizon learning.
item.dc:creator: Felix H\"ofer, H. Mete Soner

item.title: On the Depth Transfer of Neural Optimizers via L-Smoothness
item.description: arXiv:2610.14344v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scaling deep learning models efficiently requires predictable performance transfer across compute regimes. Establishing reliable hyperparameter transfer allows optimal training dynamics and structural choices to be discovered on low-cost proxy models, avoiding catastrophic failures during massive-scale training. Existing depth-transfer analyses are architecture-specific and heuristic: hyperparameter transfer is only justified through toy blocks, and both rely on infinite-depth dynamics, a specific initialization, and feature-learning criteria. Building on $L$-smoothness framework of Xu et al. (2026), we understand hyperparameter transfer as how do the Lipschitz and $L$-smoothness constants of the loss scale with the depth $K$? We show that inverse-depth residual branch scaling $\alpha=\Theta(1/K)$ is sufficient to make both constants depth-independent at fixed width, uniformly over the bounded parameter domain and for arbitrary $p\to q$ geometries. Because the bounds depend on each residual branch only through its Lipschitz and smoothness constants, the argument applies to general residual networks (including branches of block depth $\geq 2$ such as transformer and ResNet blocks) without assumptions on initialization or correlations between layer weights. Since the smoothness constant controls the curvature penalty in the descent inequality, our bounds motivate a learning-rate scale without an additional depth-dependent curvature correction for updates bounded in the prescribed norm. This provides a geometric explanation of inverse-depth residual scaling and its application to the operator-norm geometries associated with AdamW, Muon, and MOGA. Learning-rate sweeps on GPT-2 (depths 2--128) and CIFAR-100 ResNets (8--32 residual blocks) confirm that Muon and MOGA exhibit stable learning-rate transfer under these prescriptions, with a common optimal rate across a 64-fold increase in depth.
item.dc:creator: Maximilian Wong, Chenyu Xu, Jiajin Li, Yiping Lu

item.title: Deep learning from a control vantage point
item.description: arXiv:2610.14385v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This article offers an overview of recent developments in deep learning from a control vantage point. It reviews several classes of models including feedforward and residual neural networks, transformers, large-language models, and selective state space models while explaining how control theory plays an important role in understanding their training, properties, or architecture design. The article explains how residual neural networks can be interpreted as the discretization of a continuous-time control system thereby enabling the use of control theoretic techniques for its analysis. To illustrate the power of this bridge between control and deep learning, two technical results are discussed: 1) the ability of a residual neural network to approximate arbitrary continuous functions is a non-standard controllability problem that can be solved using geometric nonlinear control and 2) transformers, the key architectural component of most large language-models, can be seen the discretization of a consensus algorithm and thus large language-models exhibit consensus. Another point of contact between control theory and deep learning is the connection between backpropagation, the algorithm used to train neural networks, and optimal control. The article addresses how the older connection between these problems, established in the 80's using discrete-time models can be reconciled with the more recent approach using continuous-time models. Several open problems and directions for future research are discussed, including selective state-space models, a recent class of models inspired by the models used in control.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: IEEE Control Systems, vol. 46, no. 5, pp. 40-60, Oct. 2026
item.dc:creator: \'Alvaro Rodr\'iguez Abella, Jo\~ao Pedro Silvestre, Bahman Gharesifard, Paulo Tabuada

item.title: Entanglement-Capability-Aware Finite-Bond Circuit Cutting for Distributed Quantum Computing
item.description: arXiv:2610.14580v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Distributed quantum computing distributes workloads that exceed a single processor's capacity across resource-constrained components. Circuit cutting enables this decomposition, but its effectiveness depends on partition choice. We present SACE, a Simulation-Aware Circuit Partitioning framework with Entanglement-Capability-Aware Screening. EP-Cost screens partitions using a parameter-dependent entanglement-capability proxy and native implementation cost. Under reconstruction constraints, finite-bond refinement selects the candidate that minimizes the worst-subcircuit discrepancy between normalized MPS simulations at bond dimensions $\chi$ and $2\chi$. Across 14 exhaustively enumerated small-scale candidate spaces, EP-Cost-guided genetic algorithm selections attain co-optimal native quasiprobability decomposition (QPD) overhead, with a median within-circuit Spearman correlation of 0.9965 between EP-Cost and QPD overhead. At matched cut counts, EP-Cost reduces QPD overhead by $25.20\times$ and $16.89\times$ for 8- and 9-qubit QFT circuits, respectively, and improves sampled reconstruction. On 12-qubit approximate QFT, deterministic reconstruction reduces Pauli-observable mean absolute error in all six low-bond conditions and total-variation distance in five. With five cuts and 7,776 QPD terms, SACE is best on all four reconstruction metrics in four of six conditions. At 24 qubits, SACE improves exact-local QFT accuracy in all 30 instance-bond-dimension conditions against each EP-Cost-only, Kernighan-Lin, and spectral baseline. The 50-qubit QFT comparisons remain favorable as reference convergence improves. Weighted QAOA circuits provide complementary, more bond-sensitive evidence. Refinement benefits persist across three search methods; larger candidate panels improve the optimized proxy without guaranteeing lower exact-local error.
item.dc:creator: Weidong Liu, Qingqing Jiang, Yufu Liu, Ruiqing He, Jiandong Shang, Hengliang Guo, Qiang Chen

item.title: Ex Ante and Scenario-Conditional Value of Information in Dynamic Portfolio Choice
item.description: arXiv:2610.14821v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Portfolio decisions are often made under uncertainty about expected returns, and investors revise their beliefs as new information arrives. Although richer information generally cannot reduce optimized value ex ante, the trading strategy it induces need not improve on the strategy induced by a less informative information structure in every fixed-drift scenario. We introduce scenario-conditional expected utility and value of information to evaluate strategies selected under the investor's current belief. In a finite-horizon Gaussian portfolio choice model, we compare a fixed-belief investor, a price observer, and an attentive investor who also processes an auxiliary signal under an attention capacity constraint. Ex ante, price learning and auxiliary attention are valuable, and the total value of attention increases with capacity. Scenario-conditionally, learning creates a correction benefit by reducing the initial trading-position gap relative to the full-information strategy, but also a fluctuation cost through belief revisions, so the ex ante ranking can reverse. We derive the current-belief distribution of scenario-conditional value and the associated underperformance probability, defined as the probability of negative scenario-conditional value relative to fixed-belief choice. Over sufficiently short horizons, the scenario-conditional value of learning is negative when belief error is small relative to posterior uncertainty. For a given horizon, sufficiently high attention capacity yields a higher scenario-conditional value than any fixed finite-capacity benchmark across all drift scenarios. We also derive sharp convergence rates to full-information performance under Shannon and Tsallis technologies.
item.dc:creator: Tom Pohlschmidt, Shihao Zhu

item.title: Mixing Regularization for Average-Reward $Q$-Learning and $Q$-Planning
item.description: arXiv:2610.14988v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The average-reward setting for reinforcement learning is challenging because its Bellman operator is known to contract in span only when the underlying Markov chain is mixing. Whereas existing work typically assumes a contraction property, e.g., through environment mixing, we consider the setting where we are given a reward-agnostic $m$-step mixing policy, and we control the contraction and exploration properties of the learned policy by regularizing toward the mixing policy. We provide finite-time analysis of $Q$-learning algorithms that can be instantiated with multiple choices of regularization, with guarantees measured with respect to the regularized fixed point. Our framework exposes novel regularizer-dependent objects that control contraction, exploration, and operator bias. In the one-step setting, our rates match the best known rates for $Q$-iteration and synchronous $Q$-learning, and for $m$-step mixing we derive new rates. We also study $Q$-planning variants, and show that planning acts as time-localized learning, where the planning horizon $H$ trades off the bias from the boundary value against the sample complexity. Finally, we present numerical studies validating the analysis: (i) knowledge of a strong mixing policy improves convergence and exploration, and its advantage increases with bottleneck severity and, (ii) our theory predicts the convergence and bias rankings of regularizers from the $\alpha$-divergence family.
item.dc:creator: Julien Roger, Sam Bodmer, Jian Qian, Benjamin Riviere

item.title: Training-Free Multi-Agent Cooperative Embodied Search from Uncertain Vision-Language Priors
